name: Illinois Tech Care Hub
description: Central campus office that helps Illinois Tech students navigate food, housing, money, mental health, and emergency support. A navigator listens, then connects you to the right office or community resource.
location: Illinois Tech, Mies Campus, Chicago — phone-based
eligibilityNotes: Open to currently enrolled Illinois Tech students. No documentation required to make the first call.
recommendedNextStep: Call 1.877.351.7889 and tell the navigator what's going on in one or two sentences. Ask what the next concrete step is.

name: IIT Housing Insecurity Resources
description: Campus support for Illinois Tech students facing housing insecurity, eviction, or sudden displacement. Includes short-term emergency housing connections and case management.
contact: Office of Student Affairs — request via the Care Hub
eligibilityNotes: Currently enrolled Illinois Tech students. Bring lease or notice paperwork if you have it; not required to make contact.
recommendedNextStep: Call the Care Hub at 1.877.351.7889 and say 'I'm a student with a housing problem.' They'll route you to the housing insecurity team.

name: IIT Campus Food Resources (Hawks Nest)
description: Free food access on campus for Illinois Tech students through the Hawks Nest pantry, supported meal programs, and emergency food vouchers.
contact: Office of Student Affairs — Hawks Nest pantry
eligibilityNotes: Currently enrolled Illinois Tech students. No income proof required. Hours vary by week — check the page before you go.
recommendedNextStep: Check current Hawks Nest pickup hours on the campus food resources page, or call the Care Hub at 1.877.351.7889 if you need food today.

name: IIT International Center
description: Visa, immigration, and adjustment support for international students at Illinois Tech. Helps with status questions, employment authorization paperwork, and referrals to immigration attorneys for complex cases.
eligibilityNotes: Open to all Illinois Tech international students. Not a substitute for a licensed immigration attorney for legal questions.
recommendedNextStep: Email international@iit.edu with your full name, student ID, and one or two sentences about what you need. Replies usually come within one to two business days.

name: 211 Metro Chicago
description: Free, confidential 24/7 helpline that connects Chicago-area residents to local social services — food pantries, rental assistance, utility help, clothing closets, and more.
contact: Call 211 or text your ZIP code to 898211
location: Cook County and the broader Chicago metro area
eligibilityNotes: Open to anyone living in or near Cook County. The 211 specialist confirms eligibility for individual programs, not the helpline itself.
recommendedNextStep: Dial 211 or text your ZIP to 898211. Tell the specialist your top one or two needs and they'll narrow down options near you.

name: Greater Chicago Food Depository
description: Network of pantries, soup kitchens, and shelters across Cook County. The find-food map shows pickup sites, hours, and what to bring.
location: Cook County — many sites, find by ZIP
eligibilityNotes: Most pantries serve anyone in need; some ask for proof of address or ID. Specific requirements vary by site — check the listing.
recommendedNextStep: Open the find-food map, enter your ZIP, and pick a site open today. Bring an ID if you have one — many sites do not require it.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Free, confidential 24/7 support for people in suicidal crisis or any kind of emotional distress. You do not need to be in crisis to reach out — counselors are trained to help with anything from overwhelm to active danger.
eligibilityNotes: Open to anyone in the United States. No insurance, ID, or paperwork needed. Confidential.
recommendedNextStep: Call or text 988. You can say 'I'm struggling and not sure what I need.' That is enough to start the conversation.

name: CTA / RTA Reduced Fare Permit
description: Discounted CTA, Pace, and Metra rides for low-income riders, people with disabilities, and qualifying students through the RTA Reduced Fare program. Cuts most rides roughly in half.
location: Chicago and surrounding RTA service area
eligibilityNotes: Eligibility depends on income, age, or disability status. The RTA confirms eligibility — this tool does not.
recommendedNextStep: Visit rtachicago.org/reduced-fare to check which category fits and start the application. Have a photo ID and proof of income or status ready.

name: IIT Student Health and Wellness Center
description: Counseling and short-term mental health support for Illinois Tech students, plus referrals to longer-term community providers when needed.
contact: shwc@iit.edu — request via the Care Hub for fastest routing
eligibilityNotes: Currently enrolled Illinois Tech students. Not a 24/7 crisis line — for after-hours crisis, use 988 or 911.
recommendedNextStep: Call the Care Hub at 1.877.351.7889 and ask to be connected to the Student Health and Wellness Center. They will help you book.
